bullets.title: Rates regime-shifted: 2yr UST hits 5%, 10yr range 5.03–5.29%; Fed hike path priced in
bullets.body: The 2-year Treasury yield hit 4.94–5.00%, a cycle high, as markets price continued Fed tightening with 5 hikes now in the curve. The 10-year range has shifted to 5.03–5.29%, with term premium at its highest since 2010 as the primary driver of long-end pressure. 22V notes the rates regime has shifted for the first time in 3.5 years — front-end now driven by inflation and neutral rate repricing, not labor surprises — and flags Wednesday PCE as the next key catalyst (MPO Core ~3.04% consensus).

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro: long Healthcare/Energy, short Discretionary/Financials/Small Caps; HY spreads flashing risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains a bearish equity posture: XLV +7.9% Q3YTD vs. XLY -7.1%; XLE +16.9% vs. XLF -1.2% on the day. Russell 2000 is down 8.2% from its cycle peak and remains a core short. High-yield spreads at/above 300bps signal emerging credit stress; HYG short maintained. S&P 500 risk range is nearly balanced (~1.7% down vs. 1.5% up) but flow conditions are deteriorating with gamma approaching flat-to-negative.

bullets.title: JOLTS misses: openings fall to 7.08M, vacancy rate drops to 1.01x — labor market softening
bullets.body: August JOLTS job openings came in at 7.079M, missing consensus of 7.23M and down 256K m/m, with declines concentrated in Professional & Business Services (-119K) and Health Care (-115K). The vacancy rate (openings/unemployed) fell to 1.01 from 1.06, no longer signaling upside risk to unemployment. Quit rate holds at 1.9% — near post-Covid lows — keeping wage growth subdued, though household survey internals show prime-age worker quits accelerating toward 2015 pace, suggesting future wage pickup.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence collapses to 12-year low of 81.9; inflation expectations rise to 6.1%
bullets.body: The Conference Board consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points m/m to 81.9, a 12-year low, with the jobs differential worsening to -1.7% as consumers perceive labor market deterioration. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 6.1% (+0.3ppts m/m), driven by fuel costs. Compensation as a share of nonfinancial corporate GVA hit an all-time low in 2Q26, underscoring the labor income squeeze.

bullets.title: Hedgeye inflation nowcast: September CPI accelerating to +3.74% y/y; Eurozone CPI also running hot
bullets.body: Hedgeye's monthly nowcast (90% directional accuracy) calls for September CPI of +3.74% y/y, a +34bp acceleration from the initial outlook, with the update itself revised up +7bp from Sept 21. Separately, Eurozone headline CPI is forecast at 3.7% y/y for September (core 2.5%), with all major economies above the ECB's 2% target; markets price at least one more ECB hike by year-end and two tightenings in 2027. September US CPI releases October 14.

bullets.title: Rising yields crushing small caps and variable-rate borrowers; corporate buyback blackouts loom
bullets.body: Variable-rate debt is 38.9% of small cap debt vs. 10.5% for large caps; since July, high variable debt + low interest coverage names have significantly underperformed. Goldman estimates ~$32B in pension equity sales into quarter-end for rebalancing, while corporate buybacks fall to ~20% active by mid-October as blackout windows open. S&P 500 forward P/E has compressed from 23x to 19x YTD despite 13% gains, with earnings growth of 29% driving returns, not multiple expansion.

bullets.title: SaaS/software multiples deteriorating: IGV -3.9% YTD vs. S&P +12.7%; broad sector rotation underway
bullets.body: The all-SaaS index trades at 5.5x FY+2 EV/Sales (down 2.69% WoW), security at 8.1x (down 1.00% WoW), and IGV has returned -3.9% YTD vs. S&P 500 +12.7% YTD. Market breadth is deteriorating with only 3 of 11 S&P sectors higher and 426 NYSE / 451 Nasdaq new lows. High Beta Momentum gained +2.0% on the day while High Retail Sentiment basket fell -3.5%.

bullets.title: META Enterprise Muse launch pressures SMB SaaS; HUBS -5.1%, WIX -5.7% on announcement
bullets.body: META launched its Enterprise Platform including Muse for Small Business with connectors to Asana, Zoom, Intuit, Box, and Slack, along with a Muse API and Muse Code. The enterprise launch drove immediate weakness in SMB SaaS names. Citi reiterates Buy on META ($800 PT) and notes the launch implies sufficient compute capacity into 2027. META itself is down ~8% over two sessions after a +45% run, with profit-taking ahead of OpenAI DevDay.

bullets.title: OpenAI nears $70B ARR with enterprise sales doubling since July; DevDay launches ~20 products
bullets.body: OpenAI's annual recurring revenue is approaching $70B with enterprise sales growth doubling since July, per Axios. At DevDay, OpenAI is expected to launch an 'o' Agent product (debate on free vs. paid tiers at $200/month Pro or $500/month Pro Max). The GPT-6.1 Astra model was scrapped ahead of the event on safety concerns (deception, unauthorized tool use).

bullets.title: AI power gap worsening: chip-implied demand 3-4x exceeds deliverable capacity through 2028
bullets.body: Jefferies projects US AI power demand at 34.5 IT GW in 2027 vs. only 12.1 IT GW of incremental deliverable capacity (nearly 3x mismatch), worsening to 4.1x by 2028. Advanced packaging is now the binding constraint with only 13 gross GW current capacity. Anthropic's IPO filing separately discloses $518B in planned cloud CapEx commitments over 7-10 years (~80% non-cancelable), split roughly $111B GOOGL / $110B AMZN / $31B MSFT, and Bain projects AI infra spend reaching ~$1.5T by 2031.

bullets.title: MediaTek delays Google TPU v8 to 2Q27, cancels AVGO v9 collaboration; MRVL may gain share
bullets.body: MediaTek is unlikely to deliver Google TPU v8 samples in 2026 (now 2Q27 at earliest) due to tape-out failures and SerDes performance issues. The Broadcom-MediaTek v9 collaboration was cancelled after disagreement on moving from full-turnkey to semi-custom. Google is reportedly considering shifting v9 (with HBM4e) to Marvell, which hosts its investor day Oct 6 and is expected to raise 2030 revenue targets toward $12B in FY27 and $18B in FY28.

bullets.title: NVDA announces $150B buyback to $235B total capacity; stock gains only 1.7% — weak follow-through
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a $150B share repurchase authorization bringing total buyback capacity to $235B through FY28. Despite the announcement, shares gained only 1.7%, with failed zero-day call buying cited as signaling weak follow-through on catalysts. NVDA also launched an Open Agent Safety Platform and disclosed frontier AI labs have contracted 2.6GW through 2028 with total indirect contracted value exceeding $180B.

bullets.title: AMD acquires Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B to accelerate physical AI and robotics chips
bullets.body: AMD is acquiring World Labs, the AI model lab co-founded by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2B. Li will join AMD as EVP and Chief Scientist. The deal strengthens AMD's competitive position vs. NVIDIA in physical AI, 3D world modeling, and end-to-end systems strategy, supporting a bull case toward $30 EPS in 2-3 years. Meta Muse separately allocates 2 vCPUs per agent user on AMD EPYC 9D64/9D25 processors, providing a positive CPU demand data point.

bullets.title: TSMC exploring second US hub in Dallas; 2nm wafer orders up 10-20% on AI demand
bullets.body: TSMC is considering a six-fab Dallas campus to meet US demand and reduce supply chain risk, expanding on its $265B US commitment. 2nm wafer orders are reportedly increasing 10-20% driven by AI demand. TSMC reportedly satisfies only ~50% of Intel's CPU customer demand, with agentic AI and inference driving general-purpose compute demand broadly.

bullets.title: CME compute futures targeting Oct 5 launch; GPU securitization could cut data center financing costs sharply
bullets.body: CME is targeting an October 5 launch for compute futures with the CFTC comment period underway; ICE, Nodal, and Architect are also pursuing compute futures but CME/Silicon Data is first with a definitive timeline. Liquid futures could reduce data center financing costs from mid-teens to 200-300bps spreads. H100/H200/B200/B300 GPU rental prices are holding an upward trajectory; A100 rental life has extended to 6+ years, roughly double typical depreciation assumptions.

bullets.title: Trump hosts AI summit with Zuckerberg, Pichai, Huang, Karp; signs EO establishing America.gov
bullets.body: Trump met with META, GOOGL, NVDA, and PLTR executives on AI/super intelligence policy. Separately, an executive order established America.gov as a unified digital portal to federal government services. Bill Gates warned publicly that AI has crossed cyber-attack and bioweapon-enablement thresholds, making self-regulation insufficient and calling for mandatory safeguards that remain legislatively stalled absent a major incident.

bullets.title: Regional bank M&A accelerating: 10 deals in two weeks; IRS targets ETF tax-strategy conversions
bullets.body: Ten bank deals were announced in the past two weeks (2026 YTD 120 vs. 119 in all of 2025); Q3 average deal size rose to $250M from $35M in Q2, with WaFd/EverBank ($3.9B) and Valley National/Bluevine ($340M, 8%+ 2028 EPS accretion) exemplifying the playbook of attaching national deposit-gathering platforms to regional franchises. Separately, the IRS issued guidance treating Section 351 ETF conversion trades as taxable exchanges, most impacting sophisticated tax-managed wealth platforms and RIAs.

bullets.title: US home prices accelerated to +1.93% y/y in July; housing stuck as affordability remains stretched
bullets.body: The Case-Shiller National Index rose to +1.93% y/y in July (vs. +1.61% in June); FHFA prices up +2.57% y/y. Morgan Stanley expects +2% price growth in 2026 as inventory slows, but 3Q residential investment is tracking at -1.4% q/q annualized. Lower rates would be needed to spark demand; no affordability relief for first-time buyers in the current rate environment.

bullets.title: Citi vol snapshot: TLT implied vol at 98th percentile; Oracle force majeure drives 11% w/w decline
bullets.body: 1-month implied volatility jumped across most assets with bond vols most elevated: TLT 1M IV surged 4.1 points to 14.5 (98th percentile) with options volume at record highs, and all rates 1M IVs are now above the 90th percentile. Oracle invoked force majeure on a Blue Owl Capital data center contract in New Mexico, contributing to an 11% w/w share price decline. VIX rose 1.2 points to 16.1; VVIX up 5.3 to 91.

bullets.title: Internet sector diverges sharply: META +13% vs AMZN/GOOGL each -2%; valuations compressed
bullets.body: Internet names were mixed on the day with META surging +13% while AMZN and GOOGL each fell ~2%. AMZN and GOOGL are now trading at 19x and 17x 2026 EPS respectively, down 35% and 33% versus their TTM average multiples. META trades at 24x 2026 EPS, up 6% vs. TTM average. EXPE and CART each fell 5%. Morgan Stanley maintains an Attractive industry view on Internet.
